vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: Travellers arriving by air or sea from, or after transiting, a yellow fever endemic country (India notifies 30 in Africa and 13 in South America) must carry a valid yellow fever certificate (ICVP). Without one, the Bureau of Immigration says you will be kept in quarantine for up to 6 days. Infants below six months are excluded.

source.name: Bureau of Immigration, India — Health Regulation

vaccinations.name: Polio (OPV/IPV)
vaccinations.text: Resident nationals travelling from polio-endemic countries (Afghanistan, Nigeria, Pakistan) and from countries with imported poliovirus circulation (Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Syria) must show proof of oral polio vaccination taken at least 4 weeks before departure.

source.name: WHO — Vaccination requirements and recommendations for international travellers, country list (ITH 2022)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for India. The UK Foreign Office advises checking before you travel that you have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK FCDO — India travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: eVisa applicants must hold a return or onward ticket and sufficient funds for the stay.

source.name: Indian Visa Online — e-Visa eligibility, instructions and FAQ (Bureau of Immigration)

proofOfFunds.text: The e-Visa instructions say travellers should have sufficient money to spend during their stay in India. No official source we could read states an amount.

source.name: Indian Visa Online — e-Visa eligibility, instructions and FAQ (Bureau of Immigration)

declarations.name: Designated eVisa entry points
declarations.text: eVisa holders may enter only through the designated airports and seaports listed on the e-Visa portal (36 international airports on its checkpoint list); they may depart from any Indian immigration checkpoint.

source.name: Indian Visa Online — e-Visa eligibility, instructions and FAQ (Bureau of Immigration)

declarations.name: e-Arrival Card
declarations.text: The Bureau of Immigration says foreign nationals and OCI card holders must complete and submit the e-Arrival Card, a free service, online within 72 hours before arriving in India, at indianvisaonline.gov.in, boi.gov.in or the official 'Indian Visa Su-Swagatam' app. It is arrival information, not a visa.

source.name: Indian Visa Online (Bureau of Immigration) — e-Arrival Card form ('It is free of cost service of Indian Immigration'); the 72-hour window is in the portal's home page notice

declarations.name: Air Suvidha Self-Declaration Form
declarations.text: The Air Suvidha portal says all international passengers arriving in India must submit the Air Suvidha health self-declaration online before arrival. The Air Suvidha portal, run for the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, says the form is free, can be filled up to 72 hours before arriving, is mandatory under the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 and the Disaster Management Act, 2005, and that the registration number is shown at the health desk on landing.

source.name: Air Suvidha 2.0 — instructions for the Self-Declaration Form (Ministry of Health & Family Welfare / Ministry of Civil Aviation)

conflict.name: UK FCDO — India entry requirements
conflict.states: The form should be completed up to 24 hours before arrival.

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency notes over USD 5,000, or foreign exchange over USD 10,000 in total, must be declared to Customs on a Currency Declaration Form, according to India's customs guide for travellers. The guide says residents of India may take up to INR 25,000 in Indian currency abroad; Canada's travel advice says non-residents may not bring Indian rupees in or take them out.

source.name: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs — International Travellers: Guide for Travellers (February 2026)

The UK Foreign Office says it is illegal to possess or operate satellite phones and GPS devices in India without a licence, even in transit; devices can be confiscated and you can be fined or arrested.

safety.text: The UK warns that scammers, pickpockets and ticket touts target foreign nationals in tourist areas, and that female travellers often experience verbal and physical harassment. The UK advises against all travel within 10 km of the Pakistan border and to Jammu and Kashmir (except travel by air to and within the city of Jammu), and against all but essential travel to Manipur.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice says the monsoon season runs from June to September, when heavy rain can cause flooding and landslides across the country; the UK's says it usually runs from June to November. Canada adds that India's coastline is subject to cyclones, particularly between April and December.

tips.text: The e-Visa portal's FAQ says indianvisaonline.gov.in is the only official website for the e-Visa, and that no intermediary or travel agent is needed.
The e-Visa portal says to print your Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) and present it at the immigration checkpoint, where the eVisa is stamped in your passport.
Canada's travel advice says special permits are required to visit parts of India designated as restricted or protected areas; India's Bureau of Immigration lists them.
Canada's travel advice says travellers' diarrhoea is the most common illness affecting travellers. Its rule of thumb: boil it, cook it, peel it, or leave it.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for India?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a visa for India; they can apply online for the e-Tourist Visa (30 days, 1 year or 5 years) at indianvisaonline.gov.in. Apply at least 4 days before travel.

faq.question: How much does an India eVisa cost?
faq.answer: The 30-day e-Tourist Visa has a standard fee of 25 USD (10 USD from April to June), the 1-year version 40 USD, and the 5-year version 200 USD. Fees differ for some nationalities, and a 3% bank charge is added; the portal's fee table lists each country's fee.

faq.question: How long does the India eVisa take?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states how long an eVisa takes to process. The portal says e-Tourist and e-Business applications may be made at least 4 days before arrival and up to 120 days ahead, and that the fee must be paid at least 4 days before travel.

faq.question: Do I need vaccinations to enter India?
faq.answer: Only conditionally: a yellow fever certificate if you arrive from or transit through a yellow fever endemic country (without one you can be quarantined for up to 6 days), and a polio vaccination certificate if arriving from a polio-affected country.

faq.question: Can I extend an India eVisa?
faq.answer: No. The e-Visa portal says e-Visas are non-extendable and non-convertible. The 1-year and 5-year e-Tourist Visas allow multiple entries, with a total stay of no more than 180 days in a calendar year.
